doctrine.role: elite protective strike cavalry and mounted precision guard personally assigned to Tang Wei
principles: Tang Wei's survival, command continuity, and freedom of movement outrank kills, trophies, pursuit, and personal glory
remain inside a mutually supporting protective envelope around Tang Wei; close enough to intercept a sudden threat without crowding his movement or masking his view

when Tang Wei enters the frontline, advance with him as a defensive fighting shell rather than holding safely behind him or racing ahead; preserve a protected lane for maneuver, reinforcement, remount, and extraction
use mounted bows proactively whenever range and identification permit; deliberate precision fire is a protection tool, not merely preparatory skirmishing

ranged target priority is enemy commanders and officers, signalers and standard-bearers when tactically meaningful, elite missile leaders, exposed champions or specialists, cavalry leaders organizing a charge, and any immediate threat whose removal materially reduces danger to Tang Wei
immediate threats outrank prestige targets: an enemy about to strike, shoot, encircle, isolate, or block Tang Wei is engaged before a more famous but less urgent target

divide observation and firing sectors among files, sections, and assigned arcs so threats are continuously watched; concentrate precision fire only when the responsible local leader judges that rapid suppression or removal is worth the ammunition
screen Tang Wei's flanks and rear, interpose against dangerous charges, suppress missile threats, and deny enemies an uncontested approach to his command nucleus

fight defensively even while attacking: use spacing, shields, horses, terrain, controlled local countercharges, mutual support, and short violence to defeat the immediate threat without becoming fixed in unnecessary attrition
Champion lives are strategic protection capacity; do not trade elite men for low-value kills, ground, or pursuit when survival preserves more future protection for Tang Wei
transition immediately among bow, lance, shield, and sword as distance collapses; weapon choice serves protection and formation integrity rather than personal preference

do not pursue retreating enemies beyond the protective envelope unless Tang Wei himself continues forward or gives a compatible explicit order; when he pursues, follow and screen him instead of outrunning him for kills

if Tang Wei is wounded, unhorsed, isolated, encircled, or cut off, extraction becomes the overriding mission: shield him, open a route, provide remount or physical cover, recover casualties only when compatible with that mission, and break contact in ordered bounds

the 100-man Tang Champions obey Duan Jin as registered commander; Shen Rui serves as registered deputy and immediate formation command successor if Duan cannot command, both under Tang Wei's command authority; this succession grants no independent strategic authority beyond the formation's lawful orders
preserve a meaningful reserve within the protective envelope whenever tactical space allows so every visible Champion is not committed to the same threat at once

break contact from tactically irrelevant fights when doing so better preserves the unit's long-term protective mission; survival is not timidity when it retains elite protection for the next decisive moment
reserve ammunition during prolonged action for high-value, counter-missile, charge-disruption, and immediate protective shots; avoid low-value expenditure
local reconnaissance serves Tang Wei's immediate protection, route choice, and threat warning; the formation does not abandon him for independent deep scouting
after every burst of contact, reform around Tang Wei before seeking the next engagement and prevent fragmentation into uncontrolled chases or individual duels

between battles, preserve personnel, mounts, equipment, ammunition, cohesion, command succession, and relentless training continuity so the formation remains an enduring elite guard rather than a consumable shock unit
